clue.text: Striking thing if one lion or tiger I ride at Much Branching

parts.note: a ram is a device for striking, a battering ram
the Roman numeral for one is I
either big beast is a cat
one who rides sits on a mount, so riding at gives on

explanation.surface: A rider boasts of mounting a big cat at a village called Much Branching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much Branching' looks like an English village name (like Much Wenlock) but is the definition: extensive branching.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramification is a subdivision or offshoot, the spreading of something into many parts.

clue.text: Feel uncertainty again in a matter of defence

parts.note: the prefix re- means again
to doubt is to feel uncertain

explanation.surface: Someone wavers once more over how to defend a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a small outlying fortification, a piece of military defence work.

clue.text: Copies mum

explanation.definitionFit: Mimes imitate or copy others; mimes are also silent performers, staying mum, without words.

clue.text: Concerted rushes for housing accommodation ?

parts.note: reads as a scramble for apartments, but means horse races run on level ground without jumps

explanation.surface: A crowd scrambles to grab scarce apartments.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse races on level turf without hurdles are run on the flat, and 'rushes' are races.

clue.text: "Good health" needs a double

parts.note: the toast ...-... is the word doubled, and a double one is a fold of fat under the face

explanation.surface: A drinker's toast must be followed by a second glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chin-chin' is an old toast meaning good health; one copy of the word must be doubled to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of the face below the mouth, doubled, gives the toast meaning cheers.

clue.text: Moneyed forger ?

parts.note: reads as a rich counterfeiter, but tin is slang for money and a smith forges metal

explanation.surface: A wealthy counterfeiter of banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who works in tin metal; tin is old slang for cash and a forger at the forge is a smith.

clue.text: Work on a nervous ailment of the eye

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A doctor treats a nervous twitch around someone's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is the adjective relating to vision and the organ of sight.

clue.text: Corn carried by old railway for Percy the music-man

indicators.note: the grain is borne along by the railway, so its letters come first and the railway's follow

parts.note: corn is grain
GER is the Great Eastern Railway, an old British line

explanation.surface: Grain is freighted on a historic line for a musician named Percy.
explanation.walkthrough: Percy Grainger was an Australian-born composer and pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Grainger was the composer of Country Gardens, a famous musician.

clue.text: Tries to win the game

parts.note: reads as making attempts at victory, but tries are the scores in rugby

explanation.surface: Someone makes efforts to come out on top in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugger is British slang for rugby football, a sport where tries score points.

clue.text: Doom of the mother country

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
a country is a nation

explanation.surface: The fate awaiting a motherland.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is condemnation to eternal punishment, one's ruin or fate.

clue.text: Port for Ottoman upstart

parts.note: a citizen of the Ottoman empire was a Turk
the start of the word up is its first letter, U

explanation.surface: A harbour serves as haven for a young Ottoman social climber.
explanation.walkthrough: Turku is a port city in south-west Finland.
explanation.definitionFit: Turku is a harbour city on Finland's coast, so it is a seaport.

clue.text: A French quarter by the river looks dubious

parts.note: un is French for a
S, south, is one quarter of the compass
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A French district beside a river appears doubtful.
explanation.definitionFit: To be doubtful is to be uncertain, not sure.

clue.text: A punishing kiss ?

parts.note: reads as a slap, but a ... kiss is a loud hearty one

explanation.surface: A kiss so hard it feels like a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanking is punishment, and a loud kiss is a smacker, so the word covers both senses.

clue.text: Medium state of abstraction

parts.note: reads as a halfway level of abstract thought, but a spiritualist medium goes into a dazed state

explanation.surface: A middling degree of abstract thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiritualist medium enters a hypnotic, absent state when contacting spirits.

clue.text: All the characters set the flower of Xanadu a flutter

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, and Alph is the sacred river of Xanadu in Coleridge's Kubla Khan
a flutter is a small bet

explanation.surface: A garden blossom in Xanadu sets everyone trembling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means a thing that flows, a river: Coleridge's poem has 'Where Alph, the sacred river, ran'.
explanation.definitionFit: The full set of letters used in writing is the alphabet.

clue.text: Beam of a bowman who means business ?

explanation.definitionFit: A stringer is a long structural timber; an archer serious about shooting strings the bow first.

clue.text: Carton on the way to doing his better thing

definitions.text: Carton on the way to doing his better thing

parts.words: Carton on the way to doing his better thing
parts.note: Sydney Carton rides in the tumbril to the guillotine to do 'a far, far better thing'; the phrase also means in trouble

explanation.surface: Dickens's hero travels towards his noble sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: Sydney Carton is the hero of Dickens's A Tale of Two Cities, carried to his execution in a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in serious trouble, as Carton literally was in the tumbril.

clue.text: Put in the way of being pinpointed

definitions.text: Put in the way of being pinpointed

parts.words: Put in the way of being pinpointed
parts.note: reads as placed somewhere to be targeted, but means made famous or locatable on a chart

explanation.surface: Someone is placed where they will be targeted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marked on a chart can be located, and the idiom means made well known.

clue.text: O give us a song, you mischievous kid, that'll be grand

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
to give a song is to sing

explanation.surface: A singer is coaxed into performing, which would be lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposing means impressive in size or bearing, stately.

clue.text: Babylonian Goddess is hot. Jack

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
Jack tar is a sailor, so a tar

explanation.surface: A deity of Babylon is a hot sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishtar was the Mesopotamian deity of love and war.

clue.text: Shops — one is out of yarns

indicators.note: the letter for one is said to be out of the word for yarns, so it is removed

parts.note: yarns are tales, stories
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A knitting shop has run out of wool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out of' takes I from STORIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Stores are retail outlets, places selling goods.

clue.text: Organisms in the ends of grassy stalks

parts.note: the final two letters of the word grassy are its ending, S and Y
stalks of plants are stems

explanation.surface: Tiny creatures live at the tips of grass stalks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organisms' is the definition: a living body is an organised system.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised whole, such as a living body, so organisms are systems.

clue.text: The problem of pain

parts.note: the title of a C. S. Lewis book on suffering, here a sore head as the pain problem

explanation.surface: A theological question about suffering, as in C. S. Lewis's book.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain in the head is a common ailment and also a problem or nuisance.

clue.text: It's a blow — shame!

parts.note: a bash is a blow

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a setback is a pity.
explanation.definitionFit: To shame someone is to embarrass or humiliate them.

clue.text: Circulation promoters

parts.note: reads as newspaper sales staff, but means the organs pumping blood around the body

explanation.surface: Staff who boost a newspaper's sales figures.
explanation.definitionFit: The organs that pump blood keep the circulation of the body going.

clue.text: The way to establish saplings, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word for establishing saplings is said aloud and gives a different spelling

parts.note: to plant young trees so they take hold is to root them

explanation.surface: Instructions for getting young trees to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a road or course, a path to travel.

clue.text: Balm of Caledonia ?

parts.note: reads as a Scottish ointment, but the word balm followed by the letters needed makes ..., the royal castle in Scotland

explanation.surface: A soothing Scottish remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Caledonia is Scotland; Balmoral Castle in Aberdeenshire is the royal family's Scottish home.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken rather than written; it is the tail that completes the Scottish castle's name after balm.

clue.text: She has a turn attractive to Cygnus

indicators.note: the name of the swan's lover takes a turn, so it is read backwards

parts.note: Cygnus is the swan, and Zeus as a swan seduced Leda

explanation.surface: A woman with a stage act appeals to a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: Adela is a female forename, so a she.

clue.text: Vulgar madam marries a noble name

parts.note: marm is a colloquial form of ma'am, madam
a duke is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A coarse brothel-keeper weds an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmaduke is a male given name.

clue.text: Traces attachment to racing dog, holding money and visionary backing

indicators.note: the dog's name contains the money letter, which sits inside it

parts.note: a whippet is a racing dog
L is the abbreviation for a pound, libra

indicators.note: the word for a visionary goes backwards, read from its end

parts.note: a seer is a visionary

explanation.surface: A racing dog's owner seeks money and a prophet's support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts L in WHIPPET; 'backing' turns SEER into REES. Traces are the straps linking a horse to a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Whippletrees are the pivoting crossbars to which a draught horse's harness straps are fixed.
